relationship_type: physical manufacture candidate; likely assembly and enclosure work
evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents a Clark-labeled fuzz bearing a Manufactured and Distributed by Clark Music Industries statement, plus former Clark employee Rich Excellente describing his work wiring fuzz boxes in the company's three-man operation. The combined evidence makes Clark the strongest identified builder attribution for the Clark-branded state, while not proving Clark built every other East Coast Fuzz label.
Tone Machines found a Syracuse Herald Journal classified dated October 5, 1968 offering a used Clark Fuzz, confirming the Clark-branded pedal was in circulation by that date.

physical_builder_candidate: unknown; Clark remains strongest candidate for shared family but not proven
evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents a January 18, 1968 Cleveland retail advertisement for new Manny's Fuzz and argues for at least late-1967 commercial availability. Fuzzboxes groups Manny's with Clark, Orpheum and other East Coast Fuzz labels, but the current evidence does not prove Clark physically built the Manny's run.

Tone Machines documents a September 13, 1968 St. Louis Post-Dispatch classified for an Orpheum Fuzz and notes that prior ownership suggests it may have been commercially available before that date. Physical builder remains unresolved.

Andre Fuzzier is part of the documented East Coast Fuzz family. Similar construction and some unusual visual details have prompted investigation of a common builder, but the available evidence does not establish Clark as the physical manufacturer of Andre-branded units.
Effects Database groups MGI Fuzz with the Clark SS-600, E.U. Wurlitzer Fuzzer Buzzer, Halifax Fuzz and related East Coast Fuzz variants. Builder attribution remains unresolved.
Effects Database places AAT Fuzzier alongside Gracin's Fubar as a later three-knob East Coast Fuzz variant. No model-specific factory attribution established.
Gracin's Fubar is listed among East Coast Fuzz variants and may be connected to Bernie Gracin's New York music-store chain, but the branding itself is not enough to infer physical manufacturing.
Fuzzboxes identifies Gilsonite Music Industries of New Jersey as one of the known East Coast Fuzz branded states. Physical builder remains unresolved.
